tasks.short: Observe participants and provide corrective coaching

steps.what: Observe participants and judge corrective measures for skill improvement
Inform participants of corrective measures and check their response

tasks.design: Keep observation, correction and response checks with the instructor. Existing technique references in {DOCS} remain optional aids; this design introduces no automated movement scoring or reduction in live attention.
tasks.previous_blocker: A useful correction depends on movement, fatigue, discomfort and the person's understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: No capability in this digest establishes a safe replacement for live corrective coaching.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a cue the participant can follow and noticing when to stop rather than repeat.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor can adapt words, demonstrate differently and respond to discomfort immediately.
tasks.altitude: Time and coaching responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Recognise an exercise concern requiring the instructor

evidence.claim: Live observation and corrective feedback require contextual judgement; this unchanged workflow claims no saving.

assumptions: Boundary is live corrective coaching, not programme preparation or documentation.
Instructor produces the selected correction in s1 and observes the participant's response in s2; no structured pose data is assumed.
Review existing native reference tools before future custom work.
No new software or maintained dataset is introduced, justifying zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Class size and participant accessibility needs
research_questions: Which corrections require a pause or individual follow-up rather than a different reference aid?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100, upkeep=0, so net saving is zero. Both simple and difficult corrections retain observation and explanation time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Offer exercise alternatives for different fitness levels

steps.what: Offer alternatives during classes to accommodate different levels of fitness

tasks.design: Keep live alternatives and demonstrations with the instructor. An existing movement reference in {DOCS} can support preparation, but this task is the in-class response and keeps its time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fitness levels and tolerance can vary during the same class.
tasks.enabler_now: A list of alternatives does not remove the instructor's need to select, explain and observe them.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing an alternative that suits the person without assuming a diagnosis or ignoring discomfort.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor can change the option immediately and make participation feel acceptable.
tasks.altitude: No change to class attention or instructional responsibility.

reach.task: Support an instructor-selected accessible activity variant
reach.learn: Demonstration boundaries and when to request instructor help

evidence.claim: Offering and checking exercise alternatives during a live class remains contextual instruction rather than automatic template delivery.

assumptions: Boundary excludes advance routine planning, which is evaluated separately.
Instructor produces and demonstrates the alternative during s1; there is no machine step depending on a fitness-level field.
Native reference configuration should be considered before any future custom tool.
Zero upkeep is justified by no introduced software, scoring process or maintained library.
research_questions: Which participation barriers require an instructor conversation rather than more exercise suggestions?

already_counted.description: Select, demonstrate and check live alternatives

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100 with zero upkeep yield zero saving. Both familiar and unexpected alternatives retain explanation and response-check time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor progress and adapt exercise programmes

steps.what: Monitor participants' progress through observation and discussion
Adapt programs as needed and explain changes to participants

tasks.design: Retain progress observation, discussion and programme adaptation with the instructor. Current programmes may be referenced in {DOCS}; this design does not assume a pre-existing measurement feed or replace observation with a dashboard.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress includes technique, confidence, tolerance and personal goals rather than a single reliable score.
tasks.enabler_now: No new structured data collection is justified merely to claim a charting saving.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding when a plateau, discomfort or changing goal warrants a programme adjustment.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor can interpret feedback, revise a plan and recognise a need for qualified clinical advice.
tasks.altitude: Time and adaptation authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Communicate a participant's concern to the fitness instructor

evidence.claim: Monitoring progress and adapting exercise programmes require contextual observation; an unverified dashboard feed supplies no demonstrated labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is monitoring and adaptation, excluding separate routine document assembly.
Instructor produces progress observations in s1 before adapting in s2. No wearable readings, scored health status or structured progress record is assumed.
Check native programme-reference capabilities before custom work; existing runtime earns no saving.
No new tracking or maintained dataset is introduced, so ongoing upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How progress is currently discussed and assessed
research_questions: What information changes an instructor's adaptation decision, and how is its uncertainty handled?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0 give zero net saving. Routine progress and setbacks retain their observation and adaptation time; charting effort is not invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan routines, movements and music for participant capabilities

steps.what: Review participants' capabilities and limitations for routine planning
Choose appropriate music and movements for each set of muscles
Assemble the chosen routines and music into a session sheet
Check routines, transitions, music timing and stated alternatives

tasks.design: Configure reusable session-sheet sections in {DOCS}, with the instructor selecting movements and music from a music player {OTHER}. Reuse reduces reformatting only; capabilities, limitations, transitions and the final routine remain the instructor's decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Chosen sequence and music details are repeatedly rewritten into the same session format.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document sections and reusable tables can reduce that assembly without generating exercise advice.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing suitable load, sequence, alternatives and music for the people expected in the class.
tasks.human_edge: The instructor anticipates difficult transitions and adapts the actual session when participants respond differently.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in sheet assembly; no reduction in exercise-selection responsibility.

reach.task: Prepare a checked session-sheet draft from instructor selections
reach.learn: Sequence fidelity, timing and limits of delegated preparation

evidence.claim: Reusable document sections can reduce session-sheet formatting after an instructor selects content; this is an unmeasured fitness-planning scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is advance planning, not live coaching, progress monitoring or clinical exercise prescription.

Instructor in s1 produces planning constraints; s2 selects exact movement names, order, intended duration or repetitions, alternatives, music title/reference and timing. Full 75 hours retain interpretation, selection and capture.
Retained 6 hours of s3 include entering current session details and resolving missing selections. Reused content never supplies an inferred capability or limitation; uncertain entries remain manual.
Test native document reuse first. Music player runtime and existing templates earn no new saving; only observed repetitive assembly can shrink.
No new movement library is assumed; template upkeep is incremental. Any overlap in participant-context review with monitoring must be assigned once in a team roll-up.
unknowns: Whether session-sheet assembly currently takes measurable time
Existing native document reuse and music-use permissions
research_questions: Can a reused sheet preserve exact order, alternatives and timing while reducing formatting work?

already_counted.description: Constraint review and exact selection capture

incremental.description: Maintain sheet defaults and review reuse errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact session-sheet version with sequence, load or repetitions, timing, alternatives and music references; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100 and R=25+50+6+10=91; gross 9 less 2 upkeep gives central net 7. High requires repeated sheet assembly within the 15-hour step. Low assumes only 2 hours removed because sessions need individual rewriting, consumed by upkeep. Selection and review retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep live attention, alternatives and programme judgement; reduce a little repetitive session-sheet assembly where it exists.
reach: Guide recreation workers in preparing materials without delegating exercise suitability decisions
role.ambitious_version: An instructor who can explain and adapt a session confidently while keeping preparation clear and current.

job.title: Exercise Trainers and Group Fitness Instructors
